ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against FINTRAC-required ML/TF risk indicators, the United Nations Act sanctions and Canadian domestic sanctions lists, Special Economic Measures Act listings, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act list, and OFAC SDN data for USD-clearing/payment-platform counterparties. PEP status (including family members and close associates) triggers enhanced due diligence under PCMLTFA. No shell banks may be used, and any negative hit, beneficial-ownership discrepancy, or source-of-funds insufficiency must be resolved before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry - Corporate Registry (BC Corporate Online at bcregistry.gov.bc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be in Latin script and must include one of the legal element designations 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company' as its final element. A non-English name is accepted only if accompanied by a recognized transliteration. The name must be distinctive and not misleading under section 24 of the BC Business Corporations Act and must not be the same as, or confusingly similar to, any existing BC, extra-provincial, federal, or registered trademark protected name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting a government or royal connection: ROYAL, CROWN, PROVINCIAL, FEDERAL, MUNICIPALITY, GOVERNMENT, PARLIAMENT, MINISTRY
Regulated financial services tokens: BANK, TRUST, INSURANCE, ASSURANCE, CREDIT UNION, LOAN, DEPOSIT
Regulated professional designations: LAWYER, BARRISTER, SOLICITOR, NOTARY, ACCOUNTANT, DOCTOR, ENGINEER, ARCHITECT
Terms suggesting charitable, co-operative, or university status: CHARITY, FOUNDATION, CO-OPERATIVE, UNIVERSITY, COLLEGE, INSTITUTE
Obscene, scandalous, dishonest, or misleading terms as determined by the Registrar
Terms contrary to section 24 of the BC Business Corporations Act (name must not falsely imply specialized, governmental, or licensed status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name request is rejected, the applicant or its BC agent may submit a reconsideration application to the Registrar of Companies through BC Corporate Online together with the prescribed fee and written submissions demonstrating that the proposed name complies with section 24 of the BC Business Corporations Act. Reconsideration must be invoked promptly and in any event before the 56-day reservation (if any) expires. If the rejection is upheld, a new name reservation (and updated NUANS search) must be filed. Where statutory grounds exist, the applicant may also seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible subject to the registered office being a physical street address within British Columbia at which the company's records are available and process may be served during normal business hours; a bare post-office box or mail-forwarding-only address is not permissible. For the proposed low-risk, non-licensed OEM plush-toy operation, a professional virtual office address that satisfies the above condition is acceptable to the Registrar.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (less than 5% per annum) for an ordinary low-risk non-licensed plush-toy manufacturer; unannounced physical inspections are not a standard routine of the BC Registrar, but may occur on complaint, on FINTRAC examination, or where customs, safety-standards, or trade remedy triggers arise.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 10 (incorporation), 12 (Form 1), 14 (certificate), 27-37 (registered office), 117-139 (shares), 173-177 (directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Victoria, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1), Notice of Articles (Form 12), Articles of the ULC, and Incorporation Agreement, as prescribed by B.C. Reg. 64/2004
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under British Columbia law. A ULC may issue no-par shares for such consideration as the directors determine, and no escrow account is required unless the subscriber and Corporation agree to a deferred subscription payment. Directors must maintain solvency and disclose the unlimited liability nature of the Corporation in all contracts and share issuances.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the first board of directors of the Company, a British Columbia unlimited liability company, approves the incorporation of the Company under the Business Corporations Act (SBC 2002, c. 57) and authorizes the incorporator to file the executed Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Company adopts its Articles and Notice of Articles as filed, establishes its registered office at [registered address], and appoints [director names] as the initial directors. The board accepts the subscription for [number] Common Shares, issues such shares to the subscribers upon payment of the subscription amount, appoints [officer names] as officers, and authorizes them to open bank accounts and execute ordinary course documents. All prior acts of the incorporator are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Legal Element Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services via BCeID Online Services; Corporate Registry, Victoria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a NUANS name search through the BC Registry's authorized service provider or online portal. Select a name containing the required legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', or an approved French or English equivalent. Pay the name reservation fee and retain the reservation number for 56 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with legal element
Consent letter from existing name holder if the proposed name conflicts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If reservation is refused or queried, submit a revised name or obtain a written consent from the conflicting name holder; request administrative review if the distinction guidelines were incorrectly applied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constating Documents and Registered Office Address
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel and incorporator; no government filing required at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Articles and Notice of Articles, fixing the corporate name, registered office address, share structure, and special rights or restrictions. For a ULC, expressly state in the Articles that shareholders have unlimited liability for the Corporation's debts and liabilities. The registered office must be an address in British Columbia where the Records Office is maintained and where service of process may be made.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Agreement executed by the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Corporate Registry raises a defect in the Articles or Notice of Articles, amend the document, obtain a consent, and submit a revised filing; rely on Registry comments to cure before payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Statutory Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Incorporation Application (Form 1) via the BC Corporate Online portal, attach the Notice of Articles and Articles, and pay the applicable online filing fee by credit card or corporate debit. Mark the application as a ULC application and certify the consent of the directors and subscribers where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by the Registry, respond within the stated deadline with corrective amendments or written explanation; if rejected on legal grounds, revise the Articles and resubmit with a new filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt and Verification of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive the Certificate of Incorporation and certified Notice of Articles from the Registry. Verify that the corporate name, incorporation date, file number, registered office, and share structure exactly match the filed documents. Request certified copies and a status statement for use in banking and licensing applications.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical errors, apply for a corrected certificate or supplementary correction under the Business Corporations Act; address any substantive defect through an amendment which has retroactive effect where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organization and Initial Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors and corporate officers; no government filing beyond the optional annual report calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass the pro-forma unanimous board resolution adopting the share subscription, issuing Common Shares, appointing officers, approving the corporate seal, and opening the initial banking account. Maintain minutes and share registers in the registered office records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the initial share subscriptions lapse, obtain a new subscription and refund any amounts paid; if directors or officers decline appointment, appoint replacements by written shareholder resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Federal and Provincial Tax Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Ministry of Finance, Government of British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Corporation for a CRA Business Number, corporate income tax account, payroll account (if hiring), and GST/HST if annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000. Establish the BC Provincial Employer Health Tax account and register as an employer with WorkSafeBC. Because the ULC is a separate legal entity and may elect or adopt pass-through tax treatment under applicable rules, engage a tax adviser before filing the first T2 return.
required_dossiers: Estimated revenue and GST/HST registration worksheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or provincial authority delays the registration, follow up by written enquiry; provide supporting corporate documents and ensure all director identification information is complete; re-submit electronically in the case of a parsing error.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal or regional district planning department and British Columbia Ministry of Jobs, Economic Development and Innovation; local zoning or business-license office for manufacturing premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (Business Licence Bylaw) and conditional zoning/industrial operation permit for light assembly of textile and plush toys, including computerized embroidery and ultrasonic seaming

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment; registration under municipal sewer and solid-waste bylaws applicable to low-impact textile assembly with no toxic effluents or large emissions sources.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater discharge is expected; any floor washings, cooling water, or boiler blowdown discharged to municipal sewer must comply with municipal sewer use bylaw pH 6.0-9.0, total suspended solids <350 mg/L, and no visible sheen. Use only low-VOC or water-based adhesives containing <3% VOC where feasible; emissions of VOCs from adhesives and cleaning agents must remain below the lower-tier exemption thresholds under the BC Hazardous Waste Regulation and municipal air emission bylaws. Textile scraps, off-cuts, and packaging must be separated and sent to a permitted recycling or disposal facility; no hazardous waste stream is generated unless adhesives or clean-up solvents become waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain an occupancy fire-safety certificate from the local fire marshal under the BC Fire Code confirming egress, fire separations, and fire extinguishing equipment for manufacturing use; undergo a municipal structural load inspection if mezzanines or heavy machinery racks are installed; register with WorkSafeBC as an employer and obtain an occupational health and safety clearance, including hazard assessment for sewing, embroidery, ultrasonic seaming, and machine guarding; confirm toy safety compliance with the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act, including the Toys Regulations (SOR/2011-17), and maintain traceability records for manufacturing outputs.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) - Federal GST/HST administration and Business Number registration via Business Registration Online (BRO) and CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); provincial component for British Columbia: Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch, PST registration via BC Tax Registration portal (https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/sales-taxes/pst)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A BC ULC incorporated under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act first obtains its incorporation certificate from BC Registry Services, then registers for a 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) and a GST/HST program account (RM) through BRO, by telephone, or by mail. Required data: incorporation number, authorized representative, principal business address in Canada (or designated Canadian agent/representative for non-resident ULCs), estimated annual worldwide taxable supplies, and the anticipated date of the first taxable supply. The effective GST/HST registration date is the earlier of the date of first taxable supply or the requested date; registration is mandatory once the ULC ceases to be a small supplier or carries on a commercial activity in Canada, using the $30,000 CAD worldwide gross revenue threshold. Separately, a PST vendor registration with BC Consumer Taxation is required once the ULC exceeds $10,000 CAD of annual taxable sales sourced to British Columbia, with monthly/quarterly PST remittance and a distinct BC PST account number tied to the same BN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - For U.S. federal tax purposes, the BC ULC is eligible for check-the-box flow-through classification (disregarded entity or partnership via Form 8832), but for Canadian domestic tax purposes the ULC is a corporation and an entity-level taxpayer under the Income Tax Act, subject to full federal and provincial corporate income tax, Part I tax, and GST/HST as a separate legal person. It is neither a Territorial_Scope nor a Tax_Exempt_Zone entity; the pass-through election is cross-border only and does not affect Canadian domestic entity taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: U.S. Election: IRS Form 8832 Entity Classification Election filed within 75 days of the desired effective date to treat the BC ULC as a partnership or disregarded entity, creating a hybrid entity when combined with Canadian entity-level taxation. Canadian Elections: no domestic check-the-box regime exists; the ULC's corporate status is fixed under the ITA. Available GST/HST elections: annual/quarterly/monthly reporting frequency elections, quick method election for small suppliers, and joint filing election under subsection 225(2) ETA for closely related corporations. Foreign-entity elections: the non-resident ULC may elect under ITA Part I to file consolidated or separate foreign affiliate accrual returns as applicable. Hybrid mismatch exposure: the ULC's dual characterization is assessed against Canada's hybrid mismatch and general anti-avoidance rules (ITA ss. 18.4-18.6, 21.1, and s. 245 GAAR), which may deny deductions or recharacterize payments where the pass-through treatment results in no corresponding inclusion in the United States.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% administered by the CRA; the province of British Columbia imposes a separate 7% Provincial Sales Tax (PST) administered by the BC Ministry of Finance. There is no HST in BC; plush toy OEM sales are subject to both GST and, when made through a BC place of business or delivered to a BC consumer, PST. The ULC collects GST on taxable supplies of plush dolls in Canada and, as a manufacturer/wholesaler engaged in selling goods in BC, must register as a PST vendor.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: $30,000 CAD of annual worldwide taxable supplies (small supplier threshold; non-residents must register immediately upon commencing commercial activity in Canada even if below threshold). BC PST: $10,000 CAD of annual taxable revenue sourced to British Columbia, with registration and remittance obligations applying to manufacturers, wholesalers, and retailers of tangible personal property, including plush toys.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None mandatory. Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API clearance regime. The CRA mandates electronic filing of GST/HST returns (GST/HST NETFILE or XML EDI filing) and electronic remittance of payments above $10,000 CAD, but e-invoicing is voluntary. Pan-Canadian e-invoicing is being adopted through the PEPPOL/OASIS UBL standard primarily for procurement, and no fiscal clearance API is applicable to ISIC 3240 exports of custom plush mascots.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of plush mascots qualify for the 0% GST/HST rate where the ULC exports the goods directly to a non-resident recipient or delivers them by common carrier to a foreign destination (ETA Schedule VI, Part V). Conditions: the exporter possesses documentary evidence of export (CBSA export declaration, bill of lading, or foreign customs entry), title passes to the non-resident buyer outside Canada, the goods leave Canada within a commercially reasonable time, and no further processing occurs in Canada after export. Related offshore services, such as custom embroidery design, prototyping, ultrasonic seaming, and OEM production coordination for foreign clients, are also zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is not registered under GST/HST and who does not receive the supply in the course of a Canadian business. The ULC may claim input tax credits for all GST/HST incurred on raw materials, embroidery machinery, freight, and overhead, and any resulting net GST refund is paid by the CRA on a monthly or quarterly basis.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canadian Export Declaration (Form B13A) filed electronically through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for plush toys exported from Canada
Commercial invoice and packing list aligned with NAICS 339930 and HS code 9503.00.00 (stuffed dolls and toys)
Outbound transport document: ocean bill of lading, air waybill, Cargo Control Document (Form E29B), or courier receipt demonstrating the goods were shipped from Canada
Foreign customs/import entry evidencing landing in the destination market, such as U.S. Customs Entry Summary (CBP Form 7501)
Signed declaration from the non-resident buyer confirming non-resident status and absence of Canadian GST/HST registration, required for zero-rating of related design and embroidery services
Proof of consideration and settlement: Swift_TT inward remittance advice or Platform_Pay settlement statement linking the foreign currency receipt to the specific export sale
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA export-verification and international tax audits apply heightened scrutiny to zero-rated tangible goods exporters. If the mandatory documentation bundle is incomplete or unreliable, the 0% rate is denied, the ULC is reassessed for the uncollected 5% GST (and, for BC-destined sales, the 7% PST) plus interest, and the exporter must claw back input tax credits previously claimed on related inputs. Administrative penalties include false statements or gross negligence penalties of up to 25% of the tax amount under Excise Tax Act s. 285, monetary penalties for CERS filing failures under s. 280.1, and a standard 4-year reassessment window, which becomes unlimited where misrepresentation or fraud is established. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent export zero-rating claims can result in fines up to $25,000 and imprisonment, and the CRA may additionally cancel the BN and GST/HST program account, apply seizure or garnishment orders, and impose transfer-pricing adjustments with s. 247 penalties where the 180-day repatriation practice is persistently abused through related-party receivables.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) acting concurrently with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for banking conduct; Canada maintains no exchange-control authority in the style of SAFE or BOK because the Currency and Exchange Control Acts were liberalized in 1951.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible across both current-account and capital-account headings under a pure floating exchange-rate regime; there are no registration, licensing, or prior-approval requirements for foreign-currency remittances. Profit repatriation by a BC ULC to non-resident shareholders is constrained exclusively by Income Tax Act Part XIII withholding (statutory 25%, reduced to 15% portfolio / 5% significant-holding under the Canada-US Treaty) and, for branch-equivalent structures, Part I branch tax at 25%. No material administrative hurdles attach to the dividends or management-fee outflows provided the paying matrix is documented and the ULC files its T2/T106 information returns.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for the repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to trade foreign currency receipts through any designated bank. Export invoices for plush-toy OEM shipments may be settled in USD, EUR, or CNY and the proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency ledger accounts at Canadian banks or swept into CAD when commercially advantageous.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as a treasury supplement but not a primary settlement rail. Canada does not license standalone 'electronic money institutions' under EU-style directives; offshore EMIs (Wise Platform, Airwallex, Capital on Tap, Payoneer, Intergiro) must be FINTRAC-registered as Foreign MSBs or rely on the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) transitional licensing. Because the BC ULC is a body corporate subject to Canadian banking-privacy and PCMLTFA obligations, the core domiciliary relationship should remain with a Schedule I bank while the EMI is used for sub-CAD 10,000 vendor payables and platform-payout concentration; legal review of each EMI's Canadian registration certificate is a precondition to boarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening with video verification is permitted by most Schedule I banks for a low-risk, non-listed manufacturing entity, but for a BC ULC with non-resident US beneficial owners the prevailing practice requires: (i) one in-person meeting of at least one director/authorized signatory at a Canadian main branch, or (ii) notarized attestation plus an enhanced-due-diligence interview administered by telephone/video. Under PCMLTFA s. 11.1 the bank must verify identity using 'reliable, independent source documents', and it retains absolute discretion to demand physical board-member appearance; a director travel charter is therefore the prudent baseline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beyond-a-5% foreign UBO ownership trigger with US-based individual or corporate shareholders whose personal tax IDs are not yet on Canadian record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of passports or national photo IDs; utility bill/proof of residential address not older than 90 days; US Social Security number or Employer Identification Number; corporate existence documentation (Certificate of Good Standing from BC Registry plus Certified Translation of any foreign charter); beneficial-ownership diagram and corporate-control matrix signed by the ULC's registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Compliance officer queries the 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' naming attribute, deeming it a high-risk or unregulated shell vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written legal opinion from Canadian counsel explaining the BC ULC statute and its use as a pass-through-eligible blocker for US taxpayers; the registered-and-recorded Articles of Incorporation (Form 1/2); the latest annual report and notice of address; the actual or proposed Tax Election under s. 216/217 of the Income Tax Act where relevant; a transaction-flow narrative linking the ULC to the OEM plush-toy supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution originates from a US-based personal account of the ULC's sole beneficial owner and appears as a rapid round-number wire.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three months of bank statements for the remitting account; executed capital-subscription resolution; shareholder-loan agreement or equity subscription schedule; source-of-wealth statement (tax returns, sale-of-assets agreement, or inheritance documentation); any FINTRAC/FinCEN electronic-funds-transfer records; letter from the US CPA confirming no illicit-source nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening flags common names or prior address overlap with politically exposed persons or OFAC-listed individuals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Date-of-birth and place-of-birth clarity to resolve name collisions; copies of the individual's US passport and driver licence; OFAC-SDN and Canadian Consolidated List screenshot with negative match narrative; a notarized declaration of no legal or beneficial connection to sanctioned jurisdictions including China/Russia/Iran/Belarus/Cuba/Venezuela/Ukraine-Crimea-source materials; escalation to the global sanctions advisory unit with legal rebuttal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act (BCBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registry, Government of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after every anniversary date of incorporation or registration; if incorporated on June 15, the annual report is due by August 15 of each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to a higher late-filing fee; continued failure to file may cause the Registrar to administratively dissolve the ULC after notice, requiring an application to restore the company and payment of all outstanding fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return under the Income Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's taxation year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is June 30 of the following calendar year; for a January 31 year-end, the deadline is July 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty under subsection 162(1) is 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months, plus arrears interest; non-filing may also trigger a CRA filing demand and additional gross-receipts penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset-size audit threshold applies under BCBCA for a private unlimited liability corporation; the ULC may dispense with a statutory auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution. If a shareholder or creditor requires an audit, or if the company is a public issuer, an independent auditor licensed in British Columbia must be appointed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Canadian generally accepted accounting principles: IFRS for public issuers, or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for a private ULC; IFRS may also be adopted voluntarily or required by shareholders or lenders.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The BC annual report filing serves as the confirmation point for the ULC's corporate and beneficial-ownership information. The ULC must certify that its register of significant individuals is accurate, and upon any share transfer that creates, changes, or ends significant control, the register must be updated before the annual confirmation; the confirmation is not a public filing and is accessible only to authorized regulators, tax authorities and law enforcement.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 300–700 (approximately USD 220–520) per year for a BC registered office and mail forwarding/agent service provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No mandatory audit fee for a unanimous-consent private ULC; if an audit is voluntarily engaged, a small plush manufacturer can expect approximately CAD 5,000–10,000 (USD 3,700–7,500) for the annual statutory audit.
